chapters.title: Chapter 115 My Daughter’s Charm Is Truly Overwhelming
paragraphs: "Nonsense!" Hu Yanzhi barked, wishing he could physically kick the intruder out of the hall.
The mere presence of this country bumpkin made him feel as though the prestige of the entire banquet had been dragged through the gutter.
"Who do you think you are? A mere peasant dares to covet Pavilion Lord Yun?"
Yun He, Yun Wanqing’s father, frowned deeply. "Young friend from the Yunmiao Sect, enough of this foolishness," he said, his voice dripping with impatience.
Zhang Xian ignored the insult and cupped his hands toward Yun He.
"Uncle, the Immortal Ascension Pill your future son-in-law gifted you was quite effective, wasn't it? Surely that earns me at least a seat at the table?"
Yun He froze. He had known his daughter procured the pill for him, but he had never known the source. He turned an inquiring gaze toward Yun Wanqing.
She gave a small, graceful nod. "Father, the Immortal Ascension Pill was indeed a gift from Zhang Xian."
Yun He drew a sharp, cold breath. It seemed this "False Core" cultivator was more than just a loudmouth; he was a walking treasury.
To gift an Immortal Ascension Pill just to court his daughter? Back in the day, the Baoqing Workshop and the Great Xia Dynasty had nearly gone to war over a single one of those pills.
It seemed his daughter’s charm was truly world-shaking.
Zhang Xian finally turned his gaze to Hu Yanzhi, speaking with agonizing slowness.
"My friend, why so agitated? Since we are discussing betrothal gifts, it’s only natural to compare options. Uncle Yun, what is the approximate value of the Workshop's thirty percent share?"
"Hmph!" Hu Yanzhi was about to erupt, but his cousin, Hu Yanqing, pressed a hand onto his shoulder to keep him seated.
Hu Yanqing looked toward the Yunmiao Sect's representative. "Brother Wang Ya, does your sect usually allow juniors to disrupt such distinguished gatherings?"
Wang Ya, after a brief moment of silent amusement, offered a thin smile.

"Friend Hu, you are mistaken. This is a fair courtship between peers. How is that a disruption? Since the Baoqing Workshop has stated its price, my Yunmiao Sect must naturally show its own hand so Elder Yun can make an informed comparison."
The words were soft, but the edge was razor-sharp. Wang Ya had effectively elevated Zhang Xian’s interference to a formal competition between two great sects. Hu Yanqing’s face darkened instantly.
Yun Wanqing’s eyes sparkled. She had spent years avoiding Wang Ya's feelings, never imagining that he would stand up so firmly for Zhang Xian.
"Fine! Excellent!" Hu Yanzhi laughed, his voice cracking with rage.
"So you're the rat who tricked Brother Yang out of his Immortal Ascension Pill with a petty scheme. Let’s see what a thief like you is actually worth."
"Uncle, the calculation please," Zhang Xian repeated, ignoring the barking dog.
Seeing his daughter staring blankly at Zhang Xian, Yun He felt he owed the boy a serious answer after accepting the pill.
"I would estimate its value at roughly two hundred million mid-grade spirit stones.
Hu Yanzhi snorted. "More than that! Including the land deeds and the personnel, the market value is at least three hundred million!"
"Three hundred million mid-grade, is it?" Zhang Xian clicked his tongue and waved a dismissive hand.
"Friend, why split hairs over such petty change? I don't even carry mid-grade stones—they take up too much space. I’ll just convert it for you at the standard hundred-to-one ratio."
He paused for effect.
"Three million high-grade spirit stones. Actually, I’ll add another million just to keep it even. Four million high-grade stones. As for the betrothal gift, I’ll put down the first half right now."
"Arrogant!" Hu Yanqing sneered, shaking his head.
The other guests scoffed, treating it as a delusional boast. Only Yun Wanqing pressed her lips together, her eyes locked on Zhang Xian.
Under a barrage of mocking gazes, Zhang Xian rose and stepped into the center of the hall.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The sound of massive weight hitting the floor echoed through the room. Large, heavy chests began to pile up like small hills in the empty space before him.
With a casual wave of his hand, the lids flew open.
BOOM!
The hall was instantly drowned in a blinding, prismatic radiance. A tidal wave of pure spiritual energy erupted, so thick it felt tangible.
Inside the chests were mountain-sized stacks of high-grade spirit stones, each one pulsing with raw power.
The room went silent. The wine cup in Yun He’s hand clattered to the floor, splashing his robes.
These were the most powerful figures in the region, yet they were staring, mouths agape, completely paralyzed by the sheer wealth on display.
"There are forty chests here," Zhang Xian said, his voice calm and steady.
"Each holds fifty thousand high-grade spirit stones. Exactly two million as an initial deposit. Is this sufficient? On the wedding day, I will provide the rest in full."
He scanned the crowd, feeling a surge of satisfaction. Saving every penny had finally paid off.
Hu Yanzhi staggered back, shielding his eyes from the glow. "Impossible! Where would a wretch like you get this much money?!"
Zhang Xian offered a mocking salute.
"I truly admire Brother Hu's performance. You play the role of the 'impotent, small-minded fool' perfectly. With you as a backdrop, my gift looks even more impressive."
Pfft! Yun Wanqing, despite the gravity of the situation, couldn't help but let out a short, musical laugh.
Hu Yanzhi’s face turned a violent shade of purple. He looked like he was about to choke on his own teeth.
Zhang Xian ignored him, turning back to the stunned Yun He. "Uncle, if I may ask... what is your primary spiritual root?"
Yun He didn't even bother to correct the 'Uncle' address this time. "F-fire," he stammered.
"Perfect!" Zhang Xian clapped.

"Ephemeral Artifacts like that shield are fine, but they drain the user's essence and are gone after one use. I, your humble son-in-law, have taken the liberty of crafting something a bit more permanent."
He flicked his sleeves.
One by one, fire-attribute Spirit Treasures hit the floor.
A war-blade wreathed in eternal flames. Bracers that dripped liquid fire. Even a pair of armored shorts that radiated a scorching heat.
Zhang Xian tossed out a dozen before stopping.

"I won't bore everyone with the rest. Uncle, we can pick out the best ones in private. I’ll also throw in a few defensive treasures to handle your lightning tribulation. Consider it part of the package."
"Enough!" Hu Yanzhi roared like a wounded animal.

"You must have robbed some ancient immortal's tomb to afford this! Fine! The money and the gear—let's call it a draw! But what about her daughter’s soul? That is an incurable curse! Only the Guiyuan Sect can fix it. What can you do, peasant?"
"A draw?" Zhang Xian laughed. "Brother Hu, your skin is thicker than the Great Xia city walls. But fine, I won't argue over who's richer."
He turned to Yun Wanqing, his expression softening.
"It’s a funny thing, really. In another unnamed ancient cave, I happened to find an immortal pill. The records call it the Creation Immortal Pill.
It is designed to repair foundational damage and recreate the spark of life. Fixing a fractured soul? That should be child's play for a pill like this."
Yun Wanqing stood up so fast her chair toppled. "What? The Creation Immortal Pill?"
Her voice trembled with a mixture of disbelief and desperate, agonizing hope.
Zhang Xian met her eyes with a steady, protective gaze. "Wanqing, when have I ever lied to you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 116 The Bedroom in the Back is Also Tidy
paragraphs: For the first time, the gentle, refined mask on Hu Yanqing's face shattered. He surged to his feet, his voice booming through the hall.
"Utter nonsense! The Creation Immortal Pill is the ultimate secret of Penglai Immortal Island—a guardian treasure of their lineage! How could a junior like you possibly possess it?"
He had exposed the pill’s legendary origins in a single sentence, but Zhang Xian didn’t even bat an eyelid. He leaned back leisurely, a mocking tilt to his lips.
"My friend from the Central Continent, are you joking, or do you truly believe you are omniscient? I am not familiar with Penglai Immortal Island. This pill has a different origin entirely."
"Impossible! Take it out and let me see it!" Hu Yanqing demanded.

"My apologies, but this pill is far too precious. I fear its radiance might attract the attention of thieves. I will naturally present it to Pavilion Master Yun in private; there is no need for a 'distinguished' guest like you to appraise it."
Hu Yanzhi looked at his elder cousin, then back at Yun Wanqing. He saw her round, clear almond eyes fixed solely on Zhang Xian, intense waves of emotion churning violently in their depths.
He felt as if he were about to vomit blood and shouted to Yun Wanqing, "Miss Yun, do not listen to him! He is a fraud! Only the [Myriad Phenomena Return to Origin] can save your daughter!"
"I believe him."
Yun Wanqing's voice was soft, yet it resonated throughout the hall like a divine bell. She reined in her emotions and spoke with cold finality.
"Regarding the proposal for my daughter’s marriage—consider it canceled. The Cloud Raiment Pavilion has made its choice. There is no need to discuss this further and disturb the Emperor's banquet!"
As her words fell, a deathly silence gripped the hall.

Hu Yanzhi’s face went from a furious red to an ashen, ghostly white. The words "marriage canceled" echoed in his brain until his vision swam. He watched in agony as Yun Wanqing’s gaze moved past him without lingering for even a single second.
He had been cast aside like trash.
A feeling of unprecedented, humiliating shame flooded his body. He clenched his fists so hard his knuckles turned white, shooting Zhang Xian a look filled with pure, concentrated venom.
The festive atmosphere was dead. Yun Wanqing rose gracefully and bowed toward Xia Xuanyin.
"Your Majesty, Zhang Xian and I have... private matters to discuss. May we borrow a study?"
"Granted!" A playful glint flashed in Xia Xuanyin’s eyes.
The Emperor of the Southern Region was more than happy to see the Baoqing Workshop humiliated; the smirk at the corner of his mouth was almost impossible to suppress.
"The West Warm Pavilion happens to be vacant."
Yun Wanqing turned slightly, her silk skirt swirling like a cloud. Her gaze toward Zhang Xian held a hint of inquiry. "Shall we?"
"How could I refuse an invitation from a beauty?"
Zhang Xian stood and politely cupped his hands toward the remaining guests. "Everyone, please, continue the feast. I shall excuse myself for a moment."
As a maidservant led them out, Yun He suddenly spoke up, his voice urgent. "Qingqing, what about... these spirit stones?
The old Pavilion Master stared longingly at the mountain of treasure chests, his Adam's apple bobbing incessantly as he looked at the high-grade wealth.
Yun Wanqing paused. She glanced at the dazzling stones, a meaningful smile curling her lips.
"Father, please keep them safe for me for now."
"Oh! Oh! Right! Of course!" Yun He nodded hurriedly, then coughed several times to hide his sheer excitement at the windfall.
Hu Yanzhi could no longer contain himself. She had accepted the stones! Did that not mean she had accepted the proposal? And now they were going for a private meeting in the Emperor’s study?
"What am I? A joke?!"
He violently overturned his table, stumbling out of the hall in a blind rage, abandoning all pretense of etiquette.

The hall immediately erupted into a cacophony of whispers. No one expected this settled alliance to be snatched away by an unknown youth. By tomorrow, Hu Yanzhi would be the laughingstock of the entire Southern Region.
"Interesting." Hu Yanqing took a small sip of wine and stood up. "Today's events were... unforeseen. I shall take my leave as well."
He turned to the two Spirit Ruins Sword Sect elders who had been watching the drama.
"Elders, I have matters to discuss with your esteemed sect. Perhaps we could speak elsewhere?"
The elders were taken aback, but the other party was a Nascent Soul expert from the Guiyuan Sect; they could not refuse. "Fellow Daoist Hu, after you!"
Within moments, half the guests had departed. Xia Xuanyin turned to Wang Ya with a beaming smile.
"True Person Wang Ya, your Yunmiao Sect conceals its depths well. To produce such resources—even the Baoqing Workshop was suppressed."
Wang Ya sat in a daze, his heart a mess of complex emotions. "It was... indeed unexpected."
Strangely, he felt the death of his last shred of hope had caused his "Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra" to break through to a new level.
Inside the West Warm Pavilion, the gentle scent of eaglewood filled the air.
A maidservant at the peak of Foundation Establishment served them tea and fruits, her eyes darting between Zhang Xian and Yun Wanqing with unrestrained curiosity.
Finally, she leaned in, her voice a conspiratorial whisper.
"Please, enjoy yourselves. His Majesty has ensured the formations here are absolute; no one can spy on you. Stay as long as you wish.
She paused, her voice dropping lower. "The... bedroom in the back is also tidy and ready for use."
She bowed quickly and scurried away, leaving the two of them in total silence.
Yun Wanqing sat elegantly at the tea table, her gaze settling on Zhang Xian. "Zhang Xian, how much longer do you intend to wear that mask?"
"As far as I know, Nangong Yao is your enemy. Now that she has fled and her fate is unknown, is there still a need to hide your true face?"
Zhang Xian was taken aback; he hadn't expected her to lead with that. A faint smile touched his lips. "As expected of Pavilion Master Yun. Nothing escapes you."
He brushed his fingers over his face. The disguise rippled like water and faded, revealing his true features—handsome, sharp, and upright.
"I joined the Yunmiao Sect partly to settle the score with her," Zhang Xian admitted. "But she seemed to be an old acquaintance of yours. You won't hold it against me, will you?"
Yun Wanqing studied his real face frankly. A flicker of appreciation passed through her eyes before she shook her head.
"She was merely a nodding acquaintance introduced by my late husband. Her life or death means nothing to me."
The tension eased. Zhang Xian took a sip of tea. "Surely you didn't call me here just to see my face?"
Yun Wanqing didn't answer immediately. She looked down at the tea, watching her own reflection, before raising her eyes to lock onto his.
She scrutinized him with a gaze that felt like both an appraisal of a precious treasure and a deeply complex confession.
"I simply needed to see clearly," she said softly, her voice carrying an ethereal, detached calmness. "I needed to know what the man I am to marry actually looks like."
[Ding! Current Destiny Points: 59.] [Ding! Current Favorability: 58.]
Zhang Xian’s heart skipped a beat. Even as a seasoned "driver" who had seen countless beauties, the sight of the Southern Region's number one beauty saying such words made his Dao heart waver.
He looked into her eyes and smiled.
"Pavilion Master Yun, forgive my bluntness, but I don't sense any intention in your heart to actually accept those betrothal gifts."
The corners of her lips curved into a breathtaking arc. "Oh? You can tell?"
Of course I can, Zhang Xian thought. The system didn't give me a 'success' prompt for the spirit stones.
"It seems I guessed correctly. You have no intention of forming a marriage alliance?"
The smile faded slightly. After a moment, she smoothed a stray lock of hair behind her ear.
"In truth," she said candidly, "I never once intended to marry Hu Yanzhi."

sentences.text: For the first time, the gentle, refined mask on Hu Yanqing's face shattered.
He surged to his feet, his voice booming through the hall.
"Utter nonsense!
The Creation Immortal Pill is the ultimate secret of Penglai Immortal Island—a guardian treasure of their lineage!
How could a junior like you possibly possess it?"
He had exposed the pill’s legendary origins in a single sentence, but Zhang Xian didn’t even bat an eyelid.
He leaned back leisurely, a mocking tilt to his lips.
"My friend from the Central Continent, are you joking, or do you truly believe you are omniscient?
I am not familiar with Penglai Immortal Island.
This pill has a different origin entirely."
"Impossible!
Take it out and let me see it!" Hu Yanqing demanded.
"My apologies, but this pill is far too precious.
I fear its radiance might attract the attention of thieves.
I will naturally present it to Pavilion Master Yun in private; there is no need for a 'distinguished' guest like you to appraise it."
Hu Yanzhi looked at his elder cousin, then back at Yun Wanqing.
He saw her round, clear almond eyes fixed solely on Zhang Xian, intense waves of emotion churning violently in their depths.
He felt as if he were about to vomit blood and shouted to Yun Wanqing, "Miss Yun, do not listen to him!
He is a fraud!
Only the [Myriad Phenomena Return to Origin] can save your daughter!"
"I believe him."
Yun Wanqing's voice was soft, yet it resonated throughout the hall like a divine bell.
She reined in her emotions and spoke with cold finality.
"Regarding the proposal for my daughter’s marriage—consider it canceled.
The Cloud Raiment Pavilion has made its choice.
There is no need to discuss this further and disturb the Emperor's banquet!"
As her words fell, a deathly silence gripped the hall.
Hu Yanzhi’s face went from a furious red to an ashen, ghostly white.
The words "marriage canceled" echoed in his brain until his vision swam.
He watched in agony as Yun Wanqing’s gaze moved past him without lingering for even a single second.
He had been cast aside like trash.
A feeling of unprecedented, humiliating shame flooded his body.
He clenched his fists so hard his knuckles turned white, shooting Zhang Xian a look filled with pure, concentrated venom.
The festive atmosphere was dead.
Yun Wanqing rose gracefully and bowed toward Xia Xuanyin.
"Your Majesty, Zhang Xian and I have... private matters to discuss.
May we borrow a study?"
"Granted!" A playful glint flashed in Xia Xuanyin’s eyes.
The Emperor of the Southern Region was more than happy to see the Baoqing Workshop humiliated; the smirk at the corner of his mouth was almost impossible to suppress.
"The West Warm Pavilion happens to be vacant."
Yun Wanqing turned slightly, her silk skirt swirling like a cloud.
Her gaze toward Zhang Xian held a hint of inquiry.
"Shall we?"
"How could I refuse an invitation from a beauty?"
Zhang Xian stood and politely cupped his hands toward the remaining guests.
"Everyone, please, continue the feast.
I shall excuse myself for a moment."
As a maidservant led them out, Yun He suddenly spoke up, his voice urgent.
"Qingqing, what about... these spirit stones?
The old Pavilion Master stared longingly at the mountain of treasure chests, his Adam's apple bobbing incessantly as he looked at the high-grade wealth.
Yun Wanqing paused.
She glanced at the dazzling stones, a meaningful smile curling her lips.
"Father, please keep them safe for me for now."
"Oh!
Oh!
Right!
Of course!" Yun He nodded hurriedly, then coughed several times to hide his sheer excitement at the windfall.
Hu Yanzhi could no longer contain himself.
She had accepted the stones!
Did that not mean she had accepted the proposal?
And now they were going for a private meeting in the Emperor’s study?
"What am I?
A joke?!"
He violently overturned his table, stumbling out of the hall in a blind rage, abandoning all pretense of etiquette.
The hall immediately erupted into a cacophony of whispers.
No one expected this settled alliance to be snatched away by an unknown youth.
By tomorrow, Hu Yanzhi would be the laughingstock of the entire Southern Region.
"Interesting." Hu Yanqing took a small sip of wine and stood up.
"Today's events were... unforeseen.
I shall take my leave as well."
He turned to the two Spirit Ruins Sword Sect elders who had been watching the drama.
"Elders, I have matters to discuss with your esteemed sect.
Perhaps we could speak elsewhere?"
The elders were taken aback, but the other party was a Nascent Soul expert from the Guiyuan Sect; they could not refuse.
"Fellow Daoist Hu, after you!"
Within moments, half the guests had departed.
Xia Xuanyin turned to Wang Ya with a beaming smile.
"True Person Wang Ya, your Yunmiao Sect conceals its depths well.
To produce such resources—even the Baoqing Workshop was suppressed."
Wang Ya sat in a daze, his heart a mess of complex emotions.
"It was... indeed unexpected."

His Majesty has ensured the formations here are absolute; no one can spy on you.
Stay as long as you wish.

chapters.title: Chapter 117 I Want It All!
paragraphs: Yun Wanqing spoke slowly, her voice heavy with exhaustion.

"Over these years, the pressure from all sides—even from within my own family—has been suffocating. Agreeing to this marriage was merely a tactic, a way to retreat in order to advance. I would never surrender myself to a wastrel like Hu Yanzhi."

She sighed softly. "My plan was to propose impossible conditions. I would have demanded they cure my Zhen'er first, or asked for some mythical treasure to make them back down. I intended to use their inevitable failure to silence the public."

"And even if they actually agreed to those terms, I would have found another way to break the engagement. Hah... even if they could truly cure Zhen'er, once we entered the Baoqing Workshop and fell under their control, neither my daughter nor I would have had a good ending."
Zhang Xian inwardly praised her.
Calm, intelligent, and resilient.
To be able to strategize this far while under such crushing pressure, Yun Wanqing was no ordinary woman.

However, he recalled the System’s earlier notification: her Destiny Points had dropped by 10. Beneath this scheme, there were likely hidden traps she hadn't foreseen. But he chose not to point that out right now.

"So that's how it is," Zhang Xian shrugged, feigning nonchalance. "It seems I was being presumptuous. I thought you were actually going to marry him, so I stepped forward. Please don't blame me for meddling, Pavilion Master."

"This is different." Yun Wanqing immediately shook her head. "Although it was a strategy, it still placed me at the center of the storm. Facing behemoths like the Guiyuan Sect and the Baoqing Workshop, I am merely one woman. Even with plans, I felt like I was walking on thin ice."
She looked at him, her gaze softening. "Today, when you stepped forward without hesitation... only then did my heart truly settle. Zhang Xian, thank you for standing behind me."
Yun Wanqing’s clear eyes locked onto his. "I didn't lie to you, either. I really will marry you."
Zhang Xian glanced at her Favorability rating—58—and remained silent.

"However, I don't want our relationship to be merely a cold transaction," she continued earnestly. "Those Spirit Stones are too valuable; I must return them to you. As for my father..." A sly smile touched her lips. "I'm afraid you'll have to humor him a bit and toss him a spiritual treasure to keep him quiet."

"And most crucially," her tone became exceptionally serious, "is that Creation Immortal Pill! This item is far too precious. It might be the only thing that can resolve your False Core ailment! This is what you need most! I absolutely cannot accept it!"
"Unnecessary!"

Zhang Xian raised a hand to cut her off. "What I, Zhang Xian, give away, I never take back! Spirit Stones are just worldly dust to me—I have plenty! As for spiritual treasures? Tell me how many you want, and I’ll give you that many!"

His gaze burned as he looked at her. "As for the Creation Immortal Pill... since you said you'll marry me, then your daughter is my daughter. Isn't it only right for a father to use his resources to cure his own child?

"But!" Yun Wanqing grew anxious, her eyes filled with a mix of emotion and conflict. "How can we do that? I already owe you far too much. How can you joke about your own Dao path and future like this?!"
"Why not?"
Zhang Xian leaned forward, intentionally invading her personal space. His voice dropped to a low, magnetic rumble. "Didn't you say you were willing to marry me?"
He caught the flicker of panic in Yun Wanqing's eyes and pressed his advantage. "Or is it that Pavilion Master Yun marrying me is just a smokescreen to deceive the world? Are you not sincere?"
His gaze suddenly turned intensely aggressive. "If so, you are gravely mistaken. This marriage, I want it! You, your body, your heart... I, Zhang Xian, want it all!"
Yun Wanqing was flustered by his sudden declaration. Her heart was thrown into disarray, and her breathing quickened as she instinctively tried to lean back.
Zhang Xian's words were like a gentle yet forceful hammer blow, striking squarely at her defenses.
Yes. Whether it was the Spirit Stones, the treasures, the Immortal Ascension Pill he gave before, or the legendary Creation Immortal Pill... he had given everything.

Moreover, today in the Great Hall, he had stood before her without fear, shielding her from the storm. That profound sense of security and his unwavering support caused the sturdiest walls around Yun Wanqing's heart to quietly crumble.
Unconsciously, her gratitude was already shifting into affection.
Zhang Xian played his next card. "What? Have you forgotten your own promise? You said that as long as I found a method to save your daughter, you would be willing to pay any price."
He watched as a flush crept up Yun Wanqing's neck. "Now that the Immortal Pill is right before your eyes, does Pavilion Master Yun wish to go back on her word?"
[Ding! Current Favorability: 63.]
Yun Wanqing was left speechless. Looking at his mischievously grinning face drawing closer, she felt her heart pounding like a drum, her fingertips tingling with nervous energy.
Hearing the System's prompt, Zhang Xian laughed inwardly.
It’s in the bag!
Without further hesitation, in the moment Yun Wanqing's mind went blank, he leaned down and captured her lips.
"Mmph—!"
A warm, domineering, and irresistible sensation instantly overwhelmed Yun Wanqing's senses! She had no time to react, let alone resist.
The world seemed to dissolve around them.

Her eyes widened, filled with shock and bewilderment, before quickly being drowned out by embarrassment and a strange, electric numbness she had never experienced before. Her mind descended into chaos.
Wrapped in Zhang Xian's intense masculine aura, Yun Wanqing's body unconsciously softened. Her long eyelashes trembled incessantly as she melted into the kiss.

Only when the pressure on her lips vanished did she seem to regain her breath. A captivating blush spread across her face, dyeing her skin a deep crimson. She glared at Zhang Xian with a mix of shame and indignation.
"You... how could you..."

Zhang Xian spread his hands, smiling with extreme innocence. "Pavilion Master Yun, you wrong me! You said you would marry me. You invited me here for a private meeting. A lone man and woman in a room together—what's wrong with me kissing my future wife? Is that excessive?"
"I... I have never seen someone as... as shameless as you! No wonder!"

As if remembering something, she blurted out, "No wonder True Person Wang Ya once sent me a message, saying you were a lecherous troublemaker and that I should find time to properly educate you! Now it seems he wasn't lying at all!"
Zhang Xian didn't mind the accusation. Instead, his smile grew brighter.

"So, do you regret it now? Too late! Your father has already accepted the betrothal gifts. By tomorrow—no, tonight—the news of our marriage alliance will spread throughout the Southern Region. You've boarded my pirate ship now, and there’s no getting off."
The more casually Zhang Xian spoke, the more moved Yun Wanqing felt.

He wasn't doing this for a transaction. He was willing to give up the cure for his own condition just to save her daughter. Such a debt of gratitude... perhaps it really could only be repaid with her life and devotion.
Yun Wanqing's heart was a tumult of mixed emotions—gratitude, love, and palpitations intertwined. She whispered softly, "Then... shall we go out? You have a competition tomorrow."
Zhang Xian blinked, a teasing glint in his eyes. "Why the rush? Why don't we stay here until tomorrow morning? The effect would likely be even better."
Mischief sparkled in his gaze. "Our engagement is set in stone. If we stay here all night, I imagine Young Master Hu will be angry enough to vomit blood when he finds out!"
"You... you're so bad!"
Yun Wanqing's pretty face flushed crimson at his suggestion, and she couldn't help but chide him. However, there wasn't any real anger in her eyes. Instead, there was a hint of agreement.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 Worn Out After a Long Night
paragraphs: Zhang Xian dropped his joking demeanor, his expression turning grave.
"Isn't this exactly the outcome you wanted? It solidifies our relationship and sends a crystal-clear signal to every force watching from the shadows."
He stood up and gestured toward the inner chamber. "Alright. Go rest in the bedroom."
Rest... in the bedroom?
Yun Wanqing tensed up instantly. Was he implying that they should...

"What are you thinking about?" Zhang Xian scoffed gently, reading her mind. "I'm going to meditate out here to prepare for tomorrow's match. Hu Yanzhi hates me to the bone. When we step into the arena tomorrow, he’ll be coming with the intent to kill. I’d rather not get wiped out before I even get the chance to enter the bridal chamber."
A wave of emotion washed over Yun Wanqing. "I... I'll stay here with you."

"You'd better not. With a beauty like you by my side, I’m afraid I wouldn’t be able to control myself, let alone focus on battle prep. In my eyes, you’re a hundred times more dangerous than Hu Yanzhi."
Zhang Xian seized the moment to deliver a shamelessly cheesy line.
"I'm sorry... please give me a little more time..." Yun Wanqing’s eyes swam with tenderness.
"Just don't mind me dragging my family along," Zhang Xian laughed, unbothered. "I told you—I want you, and I want your heart. I won’t force you into anything."
Yun Wanqing felt a sweet warmth flood her chest. "You have such a glib tongue!"
Despite her scolding words, an indescribable heat welled up inside her—a feeling of security she had never experienced before.
She obediently turned and walked into the inner bedroom. The light curtains drifted shut, separating the two small spaces and providing a comforting, safe distance for both.
[Ding! Investment successful. Triggering rebate. Returned: 200 million High-Grade Spirit Stones.]
[Ding! Current Favorability: 66.]
Zhang Xian sighed inwardly. As expected of the Southern Region's wealthiest woman, her appetite was immense—she had absorbed the full investment of two million High-Grade Spirit Stones in one go.
As dawn broke, the bedroom door opened softly.

Yun Wanqing walked out, her steps light and airy. She clearly hadn't slept soundly, yet her spirits were high. When she looked at Zhang Xian, who was waiting by the door, the flicker in her eyes revealed a closeness and reliance entirely different from the day before.
"Let's go," Zhang Xian said with a faint smile.
The two walked out together.
Creak—
The maid who had been standing guard outside all night jolted awake. She stared at the pair emerging side by side, her gaze sweeping over them like a high-powered searchlight.

With a woman's innate radar, she instantly picked up on the subtle changes in their aura. She saw the faint blush on Yun Wanqing's cheeks. She sensed the thick atmosphere of rapport between them. It was the relaxed intimacy of two people who had shared a profound, private exchange.
The tea! The drama!
The maid's eyes erupted with the unprecedented fervor of a gossipmonger striking gold!
Confirmed! Absolutely confirmed!!

The Southern Region's number one Goddess! Cloud Raiment Pavilion's Lord, Yun Wanqing! And the mysterious, filthy-rich Zhang Xian! They stayed overnight in the Palace's West Warm Chamber without leaving!!
They definitely, certainly, absolutely did something beyond just talking! Otherwise, how could their eyes look like that?!

This was too much! She had to share this earth-shattering secret immediately. It was enough to vibrate the foundations of the entire Southern Region's cultivation world! She would tell everyone she knew, everyone she didn't know, and anyone with ears!
Shocking!! The Southern Region's biggest scoop! Pavilion Lord Yun Wanqing pledges her love to a mysterious tycoon! A sleepless night in the Royal Palace!
Yunmiao Sect battles Central Continent forces for the bride! Baoqing Workshop's Hu Yanzhi tragically abandoned! The prize bird has flown the coop!
The maid had already drafted the explosive headlines in her mind. She could practically hear the collective gasp of the Southern Region.

Under the maid's almost tangible, scrutinizing gaze, Zhang Xian and Yun Wanqing seemed completely unaware. An intimate energy flowed between them that outsiders couldn't penetrate as they walked calmly toward the martial arena.
Last night's confrontation and confessions had quietly drawn their hearts much closer. But in the maid's eyes, this was undoubtedly ironclad proof of the lingering afterglow of a passionate night!
The new day was destined to be turbulent.
When Zhang Xian stepped into the Yunmiao Sect's preparation area, two pairs of eyes instantly locked onto him.
"Well, well, who do we have here?"
Lin Yinyin darted in front of him, lifting her small chin defiantly. "Brother, how could you finally bear to show your true face?"

She circled halfway around him, inspecting him from head to toe. "Tsk tsk, impressive! The news from last night's palace banquet has spread like wildfire! The third round of matches finally began.

Almost all eyes were firmly fixed on the arena where Zhang Xian and Hu Yanzhi were about to face off.
A battle between love rivals! A clash of obscene wealth! The protagonists of yesterday's scandal facing off directly! This drama was just too delicious to ignore!
The entire spectator area was filled with an almost boiling, barely suppressible excitement.

"Holy crap! Yun Wanqing? She's been widowed for over two hundred years, and someone finally took her down?" The newcomer to the gossip was utterly shocked.

"Unknown?? He slapped old Master Yun He in the face with a million High-Grade Spirit Stones! I heard the old master was about to kowtow to Zhang Xian right then and there, but the Emperor desperately stopped him!"
"Two million? And High-Grade?! What on earth is this guy's background?"

"Who knows! There are rumors he's the Young Master of a super reclusive ancient clan, or the reincarnation of an Immortal. Some even say he's just a mortal who got lucky and dug up an Immortal's ancestral tomb. Anyway, he's incredibly rich now! He directly overpowered the wealth of the Guiyuan Sect and the Baoqing Workshop headquarters combined."
Discussions, exclamations, and wild theories surged through the crowd like a tidal wave.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 Qingqing and I Are Deeply in Love
paragraphs: Hu Yanzhi stepped onto the martial stage, conspicuously lacking his signature folding fan. He simply wasn’t in the mood for theatrics today.
Though he wore a mask of cold composure, a cauldron of humiliation and fury seethed just beneath the surface, smoldering in his narrowed eyes.
He glared at Zhang Xian, who had ascended the opposite side of the stage with a maddeningly relaxed air.
“Zhang Xian, you will regret this day for the rest of your miserable life! I will make you understand the true price of provoking a power from the Central Continent!”
Zhang Xian, by contrast, looked positively radiant. He took a long, lazy stretch, his joints popping in the quiet of the arena.

“Young Master Hu, you’ve got it all wrong,” Zhang Xian said, his voice a satisfied, lazy drawl. “After the... exquisite moments I enjoyed last night, I feel I could die a happy man. What is there to regret?”
“You... you two!!”
Hu Yanzhi’s face twisted into a grotesque mask. “You actually dared to commit such shameless acts within the imperial palace grounds?!”
The illicit images his mind conjured pushed him to the brink of a total mental collapse.
“Qingqing and I are deeply in love,” Zhang Xian replied, wearing an expression of wounded innocence. “When emotions take their natural course, how can it be called shameless?”
He sighed, rubbing his temples as if fighting off a lingering fatigue.
“Anyway, let’s talk less and fight more, Young Master Hu. Let’s get this over with. I’m actually quite exhausted after such a... strenuous night.”
“Aaaaaaaah!!!”
Every word was like a bucket of oil thrown into the furnace of Hu Yanzhi’s heart.
He went completely berserk, charging forward with reckless abandon. His spirit sword hissed from its sheath, bleeding a violent, crimson radiance that swelled to twice its size.
The moment Hu Yanzhi lunged, a sharp glint flashed in Zhang Xian’s eyes. He drifted backward with ghostly speed.
Simultaneously, two puppets he had poised in the shadows lunged from his flanks. Their coordination was terrifying—one aimed a lethal strike at the throat while the other swept for the hamstrings.
But the real killing blow came as Zhang Xian raised his hand. A talisman shimmering with purple lightning disintegrated into ash.
Earth-grade: Thunder Strike Talisman!
A terrifying bolt of purple lightning, thick as a wine barrel, tore through the sky and slammed toward Hu Yanzhi’s head.
This three-pronged assault was cold and calculated. Zhang Xian had been waiting for the exact moment Hu Yanzhi lost his mind!
“Hmph! I knew you’d pull a cowardly sneak attack, you old schemer!” Hu Yanzhi roared, his rage not entirely blinding his instincts.
With a sinister laugh, he flicked his wrist, activating a defensive talisman covered in ancient, profound runes.
A massive shield, as thick as a fortress wall, erupted into existence to intercept the lightning. It was another Earth-grade treasure: the Imperial Defense Talisman.
BOOM!
The formidable shield groaned under the explosion before shattering into sparks along with the lightning bolt.
Hu Yanzhi stood his ground, his spirit sword thrumming with a blood-red light that exerted a spiritual pressure equal to the weapons held by Zhang Xian’s puppets.
Clang! Clang! Two explosive collisions rang out as the blood-red blade parried both puppets, sending the heavy machines staggering back.
Hu Yanzhi stood firm, his arm tingling but his spirit soaring. The mockery in his eyes reached a fever pitch.
“Hahaha! Spirit treasures? Earth-grade talismans? You think you’re the only one with deep pockets? You want to compare wealth with me?!”
He laughed arrogantly, spittle flying from his lips.
“Zhang Xian, today I’ll show you what it means to be a mantis trying to stop a chariot! I’ll show you the price of overestimating your pathetic strength!”
“Oh?”
A hint of genuine amusement curled Zhang Xian’s lip.
“It’s true, I don’t have many Earth-grade talismans left. But dealing with trash like you? I think I can find enough to do the job.”
“Arrogant fool!”
Hu Yanzhi reached into his robes and produced a talisman shimmering with a dazzling blend of gold and crimson.

“Country bumpkin! Open your dog eyes and look closely! This is a top-tier, dual-attribute Earth-grade talisman: the Golden Flame Sky-Rending Talisman! Your shabby lightning scraps aren't fit to carry its shoes!”
The talisman ignited. Golden light and crimson flames interwove in the sky, transforming into thousands of giant sword phantoms, all aimed squarely at Zhang Xian’s heart.
Zhang Xian remained unhurried. He pulled out his own talisman, which glowed with the strange, shifting luster of watery blue and earthy yellow.
“What a coincidence. I have a dual-attribute one, too.”
He chuckled. As the light flashed, a massive, mountain-like earthen shield and a roaring water dragon manifested simultaneously.
The shield stood immovable while the agile dragon coiled around it, effortlessly swallowing the storm of golden flame swords.
Boom! Boom! Boom! Deafening explosions rocked the arena. Gold-red radiance clashed against blue-yellow brilliance in a chaotic dance of annihilation until both faded away.
Hu Yanzhi looked utterly deranged. Seeing his strike fail, he immediately flung out another crimson talisman without a second thought.
“Sky-Scorching Fire Rain!” he roared.
The talisman transformed into a crimson cloud that blanketed half the stage, pouring down a torrential rain of white-hot flames.
Zhang Xian merely flicked his finger. A deep blue talisman ignited.

A melodious dragon’s cry echoed as an ice-blue phantom soared into the sky. It opened its maw and unleashed a frigid tide that froze the fire rain into shards of ice before they could even touch the ground.
In mere minutes, the two had exchanged a dozen blows, throwing Earth-grade talismans around like they were worthless scraps of paper.
The spectators were beyond dumbfounded.
“Holy shit! Is this a duel or a money-burning contest?”
“They’ve burned through dozens already! Just one of those could buy my entire life!”
“Is this how whales fight? They aren't comparing cultivation levels—they're comparing whose family vault is deeper!”
On the viewing platform, Hu Yanqing remained composed, a confident smile playing on his lips.
He was calculating the odds: Earth-grade talismans were powerful, but they required a cultivator’s mental energy and spiritual power to command.
With Zhang Xian’s mere False Core level 3 cultivation, his reserves had to be hitting rock bottom. Meanwhile, his cousin was a Golden Core level 6 powerhouse with deep foundations.
As Zhang Xian waned, Hu Yanzhi would wax. Victory was inevitable.
Nearby, a Golden Core level 8 cultivator from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect named Xu Mo felt a chill run down his spine.
He was the next opponent for whoever won this match. He had entered the tournament with great ambition, but watching these two "burn money" made him realize how naive he was.
Whoever wins, I’m forfeiting, he thought grimly. This isn't a contest of strength; it’s a game of capital!
After another round of blinding exchanges, Hu Yanzhi realized with horror that Zhang Xian was still perfectly countering every move.
The fury in his heart was being replaced by a gnawing, cold anxiety. He didn't know how many Zhang Xian had left, but his own supply was dwindling fast.
Someone in the crowd even shouted, “Stop! The talismans you’ve burned are worth more than the champion’s prize!”
Hu Yanzhi panted heavily, his eyes fixed on Zhang Xian with murderous intent. He reached into his chest and pulled out a pill that glowed with a sinister, pulsing crimson light.
It was the Blood-Burning Realm-Breaking Pill his cousin Hu Yanqing had given him.

The pill could instantly burn his essence blood and lifespan to force his cultivation up by three levels. The cost was permanent: his Golden Core foundation would be shattered, and his path to the Dao would be severed forever.
He hadn't wanted to use it. But driven to the edge of madness by Zhang Xian’s smug face, only one thought remained.
At any cost... Zhang Xian must die!

chapters.title: Chapter 120 He Had Never Been This Powerful Before
paragraphs: Gulp! Hu Yanzhi swallowed the pill without a second's hesitation.
"Arghhh!!!"
An agonized roar ripped from his throat. Blood vessels across his body bulged violently, and a terrifying aura far surpassing the sixth level of the Golden Core exploded like a volcanic eruption.
The oppressive weight of a level nine Golden Core powerhouse swept across the entire arena, crushing the very air.
He ignited three talismans simultaneously, each wreathed in a sinister purple glow—the [Purple Ultimate Heaven-Burning Talisman]!
The three talismans transformed into world-destroying pillars of violet flame. Like three roaring fire dragons, they streaked toward Zhang Xian in a lethal triangular formation.
Zhang Xian retreated with ghostly speed, flicking out three water talismans in response. Three azure water dragons surged forward, their roars echoing as they met the purple inferno head-on.
However, Hu Yanzhi’s power had reached a frenzied peak. He personally charged into the collision, his blood-colored spirit sword erupting with a ferocious, gory radiance.
With a single slash, the bloody light blotted out the heavens.
One of the water dragons was severed cleanly by his blade, evaporating instantly into a thick mist of steam.
Moving like a bolt of crimson lightning, Hu Yanzhi delivered two more savage slashes.
He precisely struck the two golden-armored puppets pouncing from his flanks, sending them hurtling backward. Spiderweb cracks instantly spiderwebbed across the puppets' reinforced bodies.
The blood sword's momentum didn't falter. Carrying all of Hu Yanzhi’s resentment, madness, and the raw power of his burning life force, it swung toward Zhang Xian’s neck.
Hum!!
A ripple of translucent light shimmered three inches in front of Zhang Xian, halting the spirit sword in its tracks.
Hu Yanzhi’s pupils contracted. He knew Zhang Xian had already self-destructed one protective spirit treasure earlier. He hadn't expected the man to have a second one ready to go.
The time and mental effort required to refine a spirit treasure were immense; fully synchronizing with one usually took centuries of meditation.
Yet, Hu Yanzhi was past the point of reason. He roared again, spitting a mouthful of vital blood onto his blade to force its power to the absolute limit.
So what if it's a spirit treasure? I’ll cut through it all the same!!
Boom! Boom! Boom! The purple flames behind Hu Yanzhi finally shattered the remaining water dragons, crashing repeatedly against Zhang Xian’s protective barrier.
Zhang Xian was knocked back again and again, the barrier's spiritual light dimming with every impact.
"Break for me!!" Hu Yanzhi screamed, his voice hoarse. The red light billowing from his body was so dense it looked like solid gore.
His blood-colored spirit sword let out a mournful cry as cracks began to spread across its length. For this one strike, he was willing to sacrifice the weapon itself.
CRACK!!
The grating sound of shattering glass filled the air.
Zhang Xian’s protective barrier disintegrated. In that split second of vulnerability, Zhang Xian hastily ignited two earthy-yellow talismans—the [Pent-Earth Divine Shield Talisman].
Hu Yanzhi was a demon possessed. The burning essence in his veins granted him an unparalleled, albeit suicidal, strength.
With a roar of pure hatred, his blood sword shattered the two thick earthen shields in succession.
The sword light pierced the final defense without hindrance, landing a vicious, direct hit on the figure behind it.
Hu Yanzhi had never been this powerful before.
BOOM!!!
A dull explosion rocked the arena. Fragments of earthen shields flew in every direction as a massive cloud of dust swallowed the stage.
The entire arena fell into a deathly silence. Every spectator held their breath, their eyes fixed on the settling haze.
As the dust slowly cleared, Hu Yanzhi was revealed. He maintained his slashing posture, panting heavily with blood trickling from his mouth.
His eyes, however, were wide with the twisted, manic joy of a man who had finally achieved his vengeance.
Where his sword pointed, there was only a mess of pulverized stone and...
Ding!
A crisp sound echoed. A jade pendant, covered in cracks and its spiritual light extinguished, hit the ground and shattered into pieces.
It was the spent core of Zhang Xian’s protective treasure.
Meanwhile, the blood-colored spirit sword in Hu Yanzhi’s hand finally reached its limit. With a sharp snap, it disintegrated into a pile of useless scrap metal.
"HAHAHAHAHAHA!!!"
Hu Yanzhi threw his head back and laughed—a hoarse, maniacal sound that chilled the bones of everyone listening.
He had seen it up close. That detestable Zhang Xian had been annihilated by his final strike, turned into nothing but dust.
"Fight me?! I’ve left you without a corpse to bury! Reduced to ashes!! Hahaha... huh?!"
His laughter cut off abruptly.
When his triumphant gaze swept toward the viewing platform, he didn't see a heartbroken Yun Wanqing. Instead, her expression was one of tense anticipation.
Even worse, his cousin, Hu Yanqing, was frowning deeply, his lips moving frantically in a silent warning.
The dueling platform's barrier isolated the sound, but Hu Yanzhi understood the lip-reading perfectly:
Be careful.
An icy chill shot from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head. Hu Yanzhi desperately spread his spiritual sense.
At the very edge of the martial arena, a faint, maddeningly familiar aura quietly emerged.
The remaining dust finally settled.
There, in an inconspicuous corner far from the explosion’s epicenter, Zhang Xian was leisurely brushing non-existent dust from his robes.
He wore a look of "lingering fear" as he sighed. "That was close. Truly close. If that had been my real body, I’d be a dead man right now."
He opened his palm, and a crystal core slowly floated into it. He blew on it gently.
"Whew. Only the outer shell was damaged. The puppet's core crystal is intact. It’ll be as good as new after some light repairs."
The joy on Hu Yanzhi’s face froze into a mask of horror. He stared at the figure in the corner, then back at the shards of stone and jade beneath his feet.
A puppet? A substitute?
The all-out strike he had launched at the cost of his future cultivation, the destruction of his spirit sword, the burning of his very life force... had only destroyed a piece of wood?!
An indescribable sense of absurdity and rage engulfed him. He tried to raise his hand to charge again, but to his horror, his limbs wouldn't obey.
The numbness wasn't an illusion. A strange paralysis was spreading through his body.
Even moving a finger felt like lifting a mountain. Even his throat felt blocked; he couldn't even manage a whimper.
Zhang Xian’s voice, like a demon's whisper, transmitted directly into his mind.
"I mixed a little [Bone-Softening Powder] into that puppet's joints. If you hadn't depleted your spiritual power, it wouldn't have affected you. But now? You can't even surrender, can you?"
Hu Yanzhi’s pupils dilated with utter terror. He wanted to scream, to struggle, but he was as stiff as a statue.
On the viewing platform, Hu Yanqing’s face was as dark as a thundercloud. He had clearly noticed the abnormality, but he remained seated, his icy eyes locked onto Zhang Xian.
On the platform, Zhang Xian flicked his finger.
"Brother Hu, reciprocity is a virtue. Now, it’s your turn to receive a move!"
A crimson talisman, the [Li Fire Ring], instantly burned to ashes.
Whoosh!
A blazing ring of fire materialized out of thin air, encircling the paralyzed Hu Yanzhi.
The ring rapidly contracted, the terrifying heat instantly igniting his robes and scorching his flesh.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 He Was Actually Kind of Nice to Us
paragraphs: Hu Yanzhi couldn't even scream.

His vocal cords had fused in the heat. The agony wasn't merely physical; it was a spiritual flaying, his soul seared as if pressed against a red-hot iron. His body remained paralyzed, a statue of torment.

On the sidelines, the Old Steward from the Baoqing Workshop turned the color of ash. Damn the rules. He shot onto the arena like a streak of lightning, hands blurring through seals. A torrential surge of water-attribute Qi erupted, crashing down to drown the flames.
But it was too late.

The fire hadn't stopped at the skin; it was a living parasite that had surged through Hu Yanzhi’s meridians, invading his core instantly. While his exterior was charred black, the fatal blow was internal—his heart, lungs, and liver had been utterly incinerated by the Numinous Fire.
The spark of life was gone.

The Old Steward checked for breath, then sent a pulse of Qi to scan the internal damage. His eyes nearly bulged from their sockets. He whipped his head around, pointing a trembling finger at the calm figure across the stage.
"You! This is murder!!" he roared, his voice cracking with grief and fury.
Zhang Xian spread his hands, his expression the picture of innocence.

"Elder, such harsh words. He never surrendered. I assumed the Young Master of the Baoqing Workshop would have some earth-shattering trump card hidden up his sleeve. I was merely... testing the waters."
Zhang Xian glanced down at the twisted, smoking corpse. "Who knew he wouldn't even have a decent protective artifact activated? He simply stood there and let himself be burned to death."

He clicked his tongue, shaking his head with mock sympathy. "Tsk. Perhaps he felt ashamed before his ancestors and lost the will to live? A deliberate suicide to splash a little dirty water on my reputation... truly, you can't blame me for that."
"You...!" The Old Steward’s body shook violently, his aura spiking dangerously.
"Enough."
A cold voice cut through the heat of the arena like a glacial wind. It was Hu Yanqing.
The man rose slowly from the spectator stand. His gaze swept over Zhang Xian, lingering for a heavy heartbeat, before settling on the Old Steward.

"Return. In the martial arena, life and death are governed by fate. To die from a lack of skill is no one's fault but one's own." He paused, his tone dropping to absolute zero. "If there are debts to settle, we will discuss them after."
Meeting Hu Yanqing’s frigid eyes, the Old Steward’s fury was instantly doused, replaced by a bone-deep chill.
He didn't dare utter another word. "Yes, Young Master."
Bowing low, he silently scooped up Hu Yanzhi’s charred remains and retreated from the arena, a picture of dejection.
The entire venue fell into a deathly silence. The crowd was struck dumb by the bloody, brutal efficiency of the outcome.

Only Zhang Xian remained unfazed. Under the weight of countless gazes—filled with fear, wariness, or pure hatred—he calmly straightened his robes, dusted off an imaginary speck of ash, and walked off the stage.
In the spectator stands, within the Yunmiao Sect's designated section.
Gulp.
Lu Renbing and Lu Rending of Green Wood Peak exchanged a look, both swallowing hard. A simultaneous realization hit them: Zhang Xian had actually been quite kind to them.
The esteemed Young Master of the Baoqing Workshop had been turned into charcoal simply for being Zhang Xian's love rival. It was utterly deranged.

Renowned novelist Lu Renbing felt a cold sweat break out on his back. He was essentially a walking death flag. He was infatuated with Lin Yinyin, he wrote fanfiction pairing Lin Yinyin with Li Fuxi, and in his latest serialized novel, he had been relentlessly "whipping the corpse" of a villain based on Zhang Xian.
Every single one of those actions was a shortcut to the grave. He was genuinely terrified Zhang Xian would settle accounts once the tournament was over.
I have to go on hiatus, Lu Renbing decided instantly. I’ll stop updating the novel the moment we get back. Royalties are nice, but you need to be alive to spend them.
Beside him, Lu Rending was also wiping sweat from his forehead. Suddenly, his brutal training in the Nine Turns Jade Condensation Sutra—which mostly involved getting beaten up—felt very appropriate.
During the Seventy-Two Peaks Tournament, Zhang Xian had only put him in bed for half a month. That was practically mercy.

"Senior Brothers, w-what should we say?" a younger Yunmiao disciple asked tremulously. They had come hoping to see Li Fuxi dominate and watch Zhang Xian get humbled. Now, the vibe had shifted drastically.

"N-naturally, we must sing the praises of Old Devil Zha—I mean, Senior Brother Zhang!" Lu Renbing stammered, correcting himself. "Think about it. He killed the Young Master of the Baoqing Workshop and conquered the Southern Region's number one beauty. As fellow Yunmiao disciples, we share in the glory!"
"Ah! Right, right! Junior Brother Zhang is a god!!"

"Exactly!" another disciple chimed in, desperate to get on the right side of history. "If he tries to poach our sect’s goddess, we firmly oppose it. But if he chooses to 'import' a beauty from the outside? We must encourage it with all our hearts!"
By the time Zhang Xian returned to the preparation area, the other matches in his block had concluded.

Tomorrow would bring the even more brutal battles of the Western Strong block. Zhang Xian was scheduled to fight a cultivator from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect. Little did he know, his opponent was already trying to find a way to withdraw from the tournament out of sheer terror.
Zhang Xian, however, was focused on his master’s upcoming match. Li Fuxi was set to fight Yang Poxiao—a Golden Core Peak cultivator with a top-grade Fire Spiritual Root.
As soon as Li Fuxi saw Zhang Xian return, her beautiful face twisted with undisguised anger.
"For the sake of one Yun Wanqing, you’re truly willing to burn the world down?"

She stepped forward, her voice low and furious. "Do you know the Baoqing Workshop's main headquarters are in the Central Continent? You just killed the Young Master of their Southern Region branch! And right in front of his cousin, Hu Yanqing!"
Her tone held reproach, but beneath the anger was a layer of frantic anxiety.
"Hu Yanqing is an Executive Elder of the Guiyuan Sect! Do you understand the weight of those three words? Guiyuan Sect?"
She took a breath, her chest heaving. "You... you’ve placed yourself squarely in the eye of the storm! Do you think you don't have enough enemies already?!
Zhang Xian looked at her. He noted the agitation in her breathing and the faint, almost imperceptible trace of concern buried deep in her eyes.
"We already offended them at the banquet yesterday," he said calmly.
"You! You are blinded by lust!" Li Fuxi looked like she might faint from sheer exasperation.
She glared at him, her eyes swirling with complex emotions she couldn't articulate. Without another word, she spun on her heel and strode swiftly out of the preparation area.
Once Li Fuxi was gone, Lin Yinyin timely popped up at his elbow.

"Big Brother~ Don't mind Master scolding you," she said sweetly, though her eyes were calculating. "She was so nervous while you were on stage! I saw her gripping her sword hilt the entire time, her knuckles were white. I feel like if anything happened to you, Master would have rushed onto the stage to save you without a second thought."
Zhang Xian’s gaze followed Li Fuxi’s retreating figure until she disappeared through the doorway.
"I know," he murmured, his eyes softening for a fleeting moment.
After giving Lin Yinyin a quick reassurance, he walked in the direction Li Fuxi had gone.
Outside the Yunmiao Sect’s private meditation chamber, Zhang Xian gently knocked on the door.
There was no answer.
After waiting a moment, Zhang Xian pushed the door open and entered.
Li Fuxi was sitting at a low table by the window. Sensing his approach, her posture stiffened. The intimacy of the quiet room seemed to make her uneasy.
"What are you doing here?" she asked, her voice carrying a deliberate, forced aloofness.
Zhang Xian looked at the glowing [Favorability: 67] floating above her head. He almost laughed but kept his expression serious.
"I came to see my Master," he said, his voice low and gentle.

"Why see me?" Li Fuxi retorted irritably, though her gaze darted toward the window, refusing to meet his eyes. "If you have this much free time, you’d be better off thinking about your opponent tomorrow!"

A faint smile touched Zhang Xian’s lips as he walked to the table. "This disciple has his own plans. I’m actually more worried about you, Master. Yang Poxiao is a ninth-level Golden Core expert. His reputation is currently soaring."
"So what if he is Golden Core Peak?" Li Fuxi snapped, her competitive spirit flaring instantly. "I am nearly at the eighth level myself! Facing him, I am not destined to lose!"
She gripped the sword hilt at her waist, that stubborn, unyielding defiance returning to her posture.
Zhang Xian’s expression turned solemn.

"It’s not just his cultivation realm. There is a peculiar aura about him—something dangerous. He definitely holds hidden cards we haven't seen. Master, promise me you will be extremely careful tomorrow."

chapters.title: Chapter 122 The Path Narrows
paragraphs: "Master."
Zhang Xian didn't waste time with arguments. He simply flicked his wrist.
With a soft chime of displaced air, the low table between them was instantly buried under a mountain of porcelain vials, jade jars, and stacks of talismans shimmering with volatile spiritual light.

"Take them. Top-tier medicines for healing trauma and consolidating vitality," Zhang Xian said, his tone brisk. "And the Earth-grade talismans—some are for absolute defense, others for overwhelming offense. Keep them for emergencies."
Li Fuxi stared at the sheer volume of wealth he was casually tossing her way. Seeing the earnest concern burning in his eyes, the icy armor she habitually wore finally dissolved.
"The competition is tomorrow," she sighed, though her voice lacked its usual bite. "I can’t possibly refine and familiarize myself with this many talismans in a single day."

She unconsciously tightened her grip on the jade pendant hanging at her waist. "Besides, I have the defensive spirit treasure you gave me last year. I’ll be fine. As for these pills... I still have plenty left from the last time you emptied your pockets."
That defensive treasure had been practically forced upon her by Zhang Xian over a year ago. After constant nurturing, it was now nearly indistinguishable from her own aura.
Zhang Xian remained silent for a moment, deep in thought. Then, he retrieved a sleek, shuttle-shaped object and placed it firmly in front of her.
"Master, you must keep this directly on your person. Do not put it in a storage ring."
Li Fuxi looked at the object. It pulsed with a faint, rhythmic spatial distortion.

"This is a directional Void Shuttle—an Ephemeral Artifact," Zhang Xian explained gravely. "I have already bound its core signature to my own flying vessel. If you encounter a life-threatening danger, inject your spiritual energy into it immediately. It will ignore local space-locking arrays and teleport you instantly to my ship."
He paused, his eyes darkening. "If my vessel is out of range, it has a failsafe. It will tear through the void and carry you all the way back to Spirit Sword Peak at the Yunmiao Sect."
Li Fuxi drew a sharp, cold breath.

Ephemeral Artifacts capable of teleportation were rare enough to start wars over. But a directional one? One that could cross such vast distances? This wasn't just a treasure; it was a second life. Its value was incalculable.
Her instinct was to push it away. "Zhang Xian, it’s just a tournament match. There is no need for such a priceless—"
"Master!"
Zhang Xian cut her off, his voice sharper than she had ever heard it. His gaze was intense, burning with an unyielding seriousness that pinned her in place.
"Take it. Keep it on you." He stared straight into her eyes, refusing to blink.

Under that scorching stare, the refusal died in Li Fuxi’s throat. A strange warmth spread through her chest, displacing the cold anxiety of the upcoming duel. Silently, she reached out and closed her fingers around the cool surface of the shuttle.
"Alright."
"And promise me one more thing," Zhang Xian added, his expression softening slightly. "Do not push yourself beyond your limits. Do not throw your life away."
Seeing him switch from domineering tyrant to nagging worrywart in the span of a second touched the softest part of Li Fuxi’s heart.
"Don't worry," she said, her voice gentle. "If I can't win, I will admit defeat. I’m not a fool."

She offered a reassuring smile. "Besides, the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect and our Yunmiao Sect have old ties. Neither side will deliberately aim to kill. Years ago... that was my own stubbornness, my own choice to burn my foundation."
Zhang Xian studied her face for a long moment. Only when he was convinced she wasn't lying did he nod.
"Master, rest well. This disciple takes his leave."
He bowed and turned, exiting the quiet chamber.

The door clicked shut, leaving Li Fuxi alone in the silence. She looked down at the Ephemeral Artifact in her palm. A tiny point of starlight pulsed at its core, a lifeline stretching across space, tethered to him.
She slowly clenched her hand around it, feeling the weight of his protection.

For the first time in years, the crushing pressure of victory, defeat, honor, and disgrace seemed to lighten. Those obsessions were washed away by a warm current, leaving her with a strange, unfamiliar sense of peace.
Winning or losing... perhaps it wasn't the only thing that mattered anymore.
The thought made her heart tremble.

Night had draped the imperial capital in shadow.
In a private room of a high-end restaurant, hidden away from the bustle of the streets, the atmosphere was thick with the scent of expensive incense and political machinations.
When Yang Poxiao pushed the door open, Hu Yanqing was sitting at the head of the table, leisurely sipping spirit tea.
Beside him sat a woman in a provocative red dress. Her features were enchanting, her posture a blend of elegance and practiced seduction. She was pouring tea for Hu Yanqing with fluid grace.

Yang Poxiao recognized her immediately. This was Zi Xiao, the Chief Auctioneer of the Baoqing Workshop’s Southern Region branch. A Golden Core cultivator in her own right, famous for her beauty and charm. In the Southern Region, her status was comparable to a core disciple of a major sect.
"Brother Yanqing," Yang Poxiao greeted, clasping his hands. His gaze lingered on Zi Xiao for a split second before snapping back to the man who had just lost his cousin that very morning.
Hu Yanqing raised his cup, his smile perfectly maintained. It was as if Hu Yanzhi’s charred corpse had never existed.
"Junior Brother Yang, you’ve come at the right time. Sit."
Hu Yanqing personally poured a cup of tea and slid it across the table. "The agreement between us stands."
He set down the teapot, his tone casual, as if discussing the weather.

"I have already paid a visit to the two Elders from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect. I informed them that for the sake of your sword path, you wish to follow me back to the Guiyuan Sect in the Central Continent for a period of 'secluded cultivation.' Initially, they were quite displeased. After all, you are their future star."

"However," Hu Yanqing smiled thinly, "I presented them with the Ephemeral Artifact I had originally prepared for the Cloud Raiment Pavilion—the one capable of mitigating a Nascent Soul Lightning Tribulation. I offered it as... compensation for borrowing their talent."

He took a sip of tea. "Once that item was on the table, their righteous indignation vanished. Just before you arrived, I received a jade slip from their Sect Leader. They have agreed to the transfer."
A gleam of triumph flashed in Yang Poxiao’s eyes. The boulder pressing on his chest finally vanished.
"Thank you, Senior Brother, for your mediation! I will carve this favor into my heart!"

"The cultivation world, at its core, is nothing more than the strong eating the weak and the exchange of benefits," Hu Yanqing said dismissively. "The Spirit Ruins Sword Sect didn't want to agree? Fine. But do they have the strength to defy the Guiyuan Sect?"

He looked at Yang Poxiao with cold amusement. "That artifact’s value is trivial compared to a talent like you. It was merely a way to let them save face. In this world, the size of your fist is the only truth that matters.
"Senior Brother’s wisdom is profound. Poxiao understands."
"I only hope that when Junior Brother ascends to the pinnacle of the Southern Region, you won't forget your brother here," Hu Yanqing toasted.
"Of course! We brothers shall advance and retreat as one!" Yang Poxiao laughed, clinking his cup against Hu Yanqing’s.
Hu Yanqing nodded in satisfaction. He set down his cup and gestured lazily toward Zi Xiao.
"By the way. She is yours now."
Yang Poxiao blinked.

"Zi Xiao is clever, perceptive, and her cultivation is passable," Hu Yanqing said, as if describing a thoroughbred horse. "She will serve as your personal maid. She pours tea, she manages affairs, and she warms beds... she is competent enough."
Upon hearing this, Zi Xiao immediately rose. She performed a graceful, deep curtsey toward Yang Poxiao, offering him a generous view of her cleavage.
"Zi Xiao greets her Master," she said, her voice dripping with honeyed subservience. "From this day forth, I am at your disposal."
Yang Poxiao stared at her. This was the woman countless cultivators in the Southern Region dreamed of even speaking to. Now, she was being gifted to him like a piece of furniture.
He felt a rush of intoxication. This was the power of the Central Continent. This was the authority of the Guiyuan Sect.
He kept his face impassive and nodded. "I will trouble Miss Zi Xiao, then."
Zi Xiao’s eyes shimmered as she stepped forward, linking her arm through his and pressing her softness against him. "Master must treat Zi Xiao well~"

Looking at her exquisite face and the flash of her bare legs through the slit in her dress, Yang Poxiao felt a fire ignite in his belly. The sheer vanity of having such a woman fawn over him was heady stuff.
Soon, he thought. Soon I will be a true giant. And one day, I will make even the haughty Dragon Princess, Long Zhi, bow her head to me.
Hu Yanqing tapped his fingers on the table, the rhythmic sound pulling Yang Poxiao back to reality.
"Poxiao. There is one small matter this Senior Brother needs your help with."
Yang Poxiao’s expression hardened. "Is it Zhang Xian? Do you want me to find an opportunity to kill him in the arena?"
"No."
Hu Yanqing shook his head slowly, a smile playing on his lips that didn't reach his eyes.

"That kid... his methods are bizarre. He throws around wealth like water and possesses strange artifacts. Killing him in the arena is too risky; he’s a cockroach that’s hard to squash. I don’t want to put you in a difficult position."
Hu Yanqing leaned forward, his eyes suddenly sharpening into needle points.
"I want you to settle for the next best thing."
"Tomorrow, you face Li Fuxi."
"I want you to destroy her. Do not just defeat her—injure her foundation. Shatter her Dao. Make sure she is so broken that she can never resist again."

chapters.title: Chapter 123 Master Is Being Stubborn Again
paragraphs: "Li Fuxi?"
A cold, cruel smile tugged at the corner of Yang Poxiao's mouth. "A mere seventh-stage Golden Core is no match for me. Breaking her will be trivial."
He paused, his eyes glinting with icy malice. "Besides, her relationship with that Zhang Xian seems... rather ambiguous. It’s perfect. I have old debts to settle with him anyway."
"Oh?" Hu Yanqing’s interest peaked. "Old debts?"
Yang Poxiao snorted, a flash of genuine anger crossing his face. "Firstly, avenging Brother Yanzhi is my duty. Secondly..."

He gritted his teeth. "I only learned today that it was him who, back then, swindled me out of two Immortal Ascension Pills in exchange for a single stalk of Immortal Ascension Herb! That's how he curried favor with the Cloud Raiment Pavilion."
Of course, he didn't voice the deepest, darkest reason: any man who dared to show closeness or desire toward his master, Long Zhi, deserved nothing less than death.
A look of approval appeared on Hu Yanqing's face. "Excellent! A personal vendetta makes the wine taste sweeter."
A glint of triumphant scheming flashed deep in his eyes, as if he could already see Li Fuxi lying broken and bloody on the arena floor.
If Yang Poxiao can seriously injure Li Fuxi, shattering her foundation and leaving her powerless to resist... then I, representing the Guiyuan Sect, can step in at the perfect moment.
I will magnanimously offer aid, inviting her back to the sect for 'careful treatment.' At that point, this woman will be entirely in my hands. To heal, to indebt, to own... it will all be up to me.
The next day, the Martial Arts Plaza.
The crowd was even more massive and turbulent than the day before. The excitement in the air was thick enough to choke on.

Zhang Xian's opponent was Xu Mo, an eighth-stage Golden Core cultivator from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect. Having witnessed Zhang Xian's pay-to-win massacre of Hu Yanzhi yesterday, Xu Mo now stood on the arena platform with a face the color of old parchment.
There was very little fighting spirit left in his eyes.

"Fellow Daoist Zhang, I seek your guidance," Xu Mo forced out a cupped-fist salute. He thought for a moment and decided to adopt a purely defensive stance. What if my opponent exhausted his stockpile of nukes yesterday? I just need to survive.
Zhang Xian, however, was preoccupied. His mind was entirely focused on his master Li Fuxi's upcoming match on the adjacent stage. He had zero desire to prolong this farce.
Without a word, he flicked his sleeve. Two battle puppets shot out, instantly engulfing Xu Mo in a storm of relentless attacks.

Though Xu Mo's heart was filled with trepidation, he was still an elite disciple of the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect. His swordsmanship was exquisite, and for a time, he managed to defend himself flawlessly against the mechanical onslaught.
However, Zhang Xian's puppets were empowered by spirit treasures. They unleashed wave after wave of increasingly ferocious assaults, gradually suffocating Xu Mo's defenses.

After just a few exchanges, Xu Mo was sweating profusely, inwardly cursing his misfortune. He noticed Zhang Xian's gaze frequently drifting toward the neighboring arena, clearly indicating his mind wasn't on this fight at all.
This won't do! I'm bound to lose if this continues!
Gritting his teeth, Xu Mo prepared to unleash his trump card—a secret sword formation technique—for a desperate, all-out gamble.
Just then, Zhang Xian frowned slightly. He seemed annoyed by the delay.
With a flip of his fingers, two talismans instantly appeared between them.
Lightning coiled around the paper, radiating a heart-palpitating aura of destruction. They were, unmistakably, two more Earth-grade Thunder Talismans.
Holy shit!!
Xu Mo's scalp instantly went numb. The horrific memory of Hu Yanzhi being blasted by those very same talismans yesterday was still vivid in his mind. He dared not even think about tanking that.
"I concede!!!"
Xu Mo practically shrieked the words. He leaped backward, throwing himself off the arena platform before the talismans could even ignite.
The referee was momentarily stunned before announcing, "Yunmiao Sect, Zhang Xian wins!"
Without even a glance at the fleeing Xu Mo, Zhang Xian's figure blurred as he flashed to the edge of the neighboring arena where Li Fuxi and Yang Poxiao were fighting.
The moment he arrived, the deafening sound of clashing energies assaulted his senses.
On the platform, Li Fuxi moved with the grace of a celestial maiden. Twin swords danced in her hands—one azure as ice, the other gleaming with brilliant golden light.

The two blades transformed into streams of liquid light in her grasp, the softness of Water and the hardness of Metal merging perfectly. The sword intents of the Yunmiao Sect's Yunmiao Sword Scripture and the Heavenly Palace Azure Cloud Sword were displayed to their absolute limit.
Her opponent, Yang Poxiao, was like a fiery god of war.
He wielded a massive crimson greatsword. His Supreme Fire Spirit Root granted him savage, unmatched power. Every slash carried the might to scorch mountains and boil seas.
Their battle was intensely fierce. Sword energy crisscrossed, flames shot toward the sky, and the spectators below cheered with exhilaration.
"Now this is a true peak showdown!"
"Brilliant! Far better to watch than those two pay-to-win tycoons fighting yesterday!"
The audience watched, enthralled. This was the kind of contest they had been waiting for—skill against skill, power against power. What honor was there in just throwing money around?
However, Zhang Xian noticed something amiss. Other cultivators with keen eyesight saw it too.
The scales of victory were slowly tilting in Yang Poxiao's favor.
Though Li Fuxi possessed exceptional talent, dual Supreme Spirit Roots, and wielded two spirit treasure-grade flying swords, she was ultimately only at the seventh stage of Golden Core.

Yang Poxiao was a genuine Golden Core Peak cultivator. The chasm in cultivation realm was not something easily bridged. More crucially, Yang Poxiao's greatsword was also spirit treasure-grade. In terms of weaponry, Li Fuxi held no advantage.

Regarding swordsmanship, Li Fuxi's techniques were exquisite and endlessly varied. But Yang Poxiao hailed from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect, where the Sword Dao was their religion. In terms of pure swordsmanship finesse, the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect even surpassed the Yunmiao Sect.

His foundation was incredibly solid. Within his broad, sweeping strokes lay the simplest yet strongest principles of the sword. When defending, he was as immovable as a boulder; when attacking, he erupted like a volcano. Li Fuxi's intricate sword moves were often dismantled by his force-over-finesse momentum.

Zhang Xian couldn't help but marvel. He understood his master's current strength better than anyone. Dual Supreme Spirit Roots, two offensive spirit treasures, the heightened comprehension from daily Qingqiao tea... such a configuration was enough to utterly dominate ordinary peak Golden Core cultivators.

Yet Yang Poxiao still steadily held the upper hand. Though Li Fuxi's sword intent was peerlessly sharp, it consistently failed to break through Yang Poxiao's seemingly simple, yet impenetrable, defense.
This Yang Poxiao... fellow transmigrator that he is, really does have some skills.

Time passed minute by minute. Li Fuxi's offensive remained fierce, but Zhang Xian keenly sensed her breathing rhythm beginning to quicken. Fine beads of sweat appeared at her temples. The spiritual power within her was nearly depleted.
Li Fuxi felt it herself. She took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing her churning Qi and blood. The thought of retreat already sprouted in her mind.
Forget it. This battle is beyond my current strength. I should concede.
Even Zhang Xian could see his master was ready to give up and secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
Suddenly, an abrupt change occurred.
In the midst of the fierce exchange, Li Fuxi shuddered violently, as if struck by an invisible blow. Her face instantly turned deathly pale, and even her sword-gripping hand trembled.
Across from her, Yang Poxiao chose that exact moment to suddenly sheathe his sword and stand still. A faint, mocking smile played on his lips.
Something's wrong! Zhang Xian's heart gave a violent lurch.
The next second, Li Fuxi sharply raised her head. Her gaze didn't land on Yang Poxiao but pierced through the crowd, fixing directly on Zhang Xian.
That look in her eyes was indescribably complex. There was worry, fear, and a trace of desperate resolve.

Then, without the slightest hesitation, Li Fuxi pulled out a pill radiating with immense vitality—precisely the High-Grade Spirit Recovery Pill Zhang Xian had given her earlier—and swallowed it in one gulp.
Master is being stubborn again!?
No!
In that lightning-fast instant, Zhang Xian realized the truth. Master was clearly ready to concede just a moment ago. Why would she suddenly decide to fight desperately now?
Zhang Xian's gaze instantly locked onto the triumphant smirk curling at the corner of Yang Poxiao's mouth.
It's him! Master must have discovered something... or he secretly sent her a voice transmission to trigger her!
